source.text: Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους, καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν. καὶ λέγει μοι· Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ· τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. 2. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάγον ἔρχονται, καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς· κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν [καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν], καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν , καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. 3. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς· ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ· ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. 4. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ Κυρίου ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν. ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες· ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. 5. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ Θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος. 6. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον· καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. 7. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text:
1[2]. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me, “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful; and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.

2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them; and that false prophet[4], having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they desire.

3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.

4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.

5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.

6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.

7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.

8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.

9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.

10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.

11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty and has no power, but is foolish.

12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.

14. [Heaven.] 

19. “How,” I say, “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.” “As these, then, are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.

20. Take now the power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a man’s head, how much pain it causes! Or again, take a drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground, and it bores through the stone.

21. You see, then, that things from above, though very small when they fall upon the earth, have great power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust in this spirit[a][21][14][10][9][8], but keep away from the other.”

footnotes.text: The bracketed clause “and according to the desires of their wickedness” is marked as secondary by some editors; the Greek source layer flags it as editorially uncertain.
“Like the nations” refers to pagan peoples (Gentiles) and their divinatory practices.
“Nor does he speak in private” renders κατὰ μόνας (“when alone/privately”). The point is that true prophecy is not dispensed on demand in private consultation.
“Angel of the prophetic spirit” reflects Hermas’s angelology, in which angelic beings oversee aspects of divine revelation and community life.
“The Deity” translates θεότης, a rare term also found in Col 2:9. It denotes divine nature/essence, not merely ‘divineness.’
The source layer preserves only the single word “heaven.” Most editions supply several lines here with two illustrative impossibilities; the omission likely reflects a lacuna in this OCR layer.
The contrast between things “from above” and “earthly” runs through this Mandate, culminating in the hail and drip images to illustrate true (from above) versus false (earthly) spirits.
Or 'For every spirit given from God is not consulted'.

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God. Preserve the adverse direction.

lexical_decisions.rationale: A low shared seat; “bench” captures a communal sitting surface distinguished from a single chair (καθέδρα).
Concrete furniture term; “chair” contrasts with the bench and underscores the false prophet’s singled‑out position.
Standard, transparent rendering for a claimant to prophecy who is false.
In context, what is being ruined is the capacity to judge rightly; “understanding” fits well.
Project default prefers “slaves” where belonging to God is salient; Hermas emphasizes divine ownership.
Established moral term in Hermas; “double‑minded” preserves idiom and his recurring vice list.
Hermas contrasts prophecy with divinatory magic; “magician” is the clearest modern equivalent.
In context of seeking future knowledge from a seer; “consult” communicates the divinatory act.

lexical_decisions.chosen: divine spirit / the spirit of the Deity
lexical_decisions.rationale: Hermas distinguishes adjectives (theios vs. hagios). Rendering preserves the nuance of divinity/Deity.
Retains adjective “holy” explicitly; capitalization lightly varied to reflect Greek adjective, not a proper name.
Key motif (emptiness) contrasted with fullness of the divine spirit; keep consistent literal term.
Violent metaphor for pulling some of the righteous away; “tear away” is vivid yet accurate.
Clothing metaphor is important in Hermas; “put on” preserves the verb.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Recorded source/witness and contextual review; see docs/REPENTANCE_REASSESSMENT_2026-10-13.md
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God. Preserve the adverse direction. Contextual editorial assessment, not independent scholarly certification.
Pagan divinatory practice; “practice divination” is precise.
Verbal form; “worship idols” keeps active sense that incurs guilt.
“Deity” is transparent and contemporary while retaining metaphysical weight; avoids archaic “Godhead.”
Formal communal prayer; “petition” fits the setting of a gathering appealing to God.

alternatives: angel assigned to the prophetic spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literal rendering preserves Hermas’s angelology linking prophetic inspiration with angelic oversight.
Moral self‑promotion opposed to humility; “exalts himself” echoes biblical idiom without importing NT phrasing unduly.
Conveys forward, rash boldness fitting the false prophet’s demeanor.
Moral lack of shame is in view; “shameless” is clear.
Describes verbosity; “talkative” is simple and accurate.
Lifestyle of ease and indulgence; “luxury” fits plural “many luxuries.”
General term for deceptive practices.
Remuneration received for prophecy; “payment” covers the sense without implying employment (wages).
General assembly; avoids anachronistic association with the Jewish synagogue while keeping literal sense.
Concrete image of skulking prophecy away from the gathered righteous; literal but intelligible.
“Agree with one another” fits the vessel metaphor plainly.
Captures lack of effective power; pairs well with “earthly” and “light.”
Collective used as countable in context; “hail” as a small pellet is familiar.
Ceramic roofing tile in Greco‑Roman context; “roof tile” specifies origin of the drop.
Simple, literal rendering.
Describes the erosive effect of repeated drops; “bores through” is vivid and idiomatic.
Retains the sense of a gathered many to whom the inspired person speaks.
Primary meaning is light (in weight); connotes triviality; kept literal with context clarifying weakness.
Genitive likely objective (“in”); chosen for clarity, with alternatives noted in theological decisions.

Modern Hermas commentary and translation literature (consult only)
Secondary Latin / Ethiopic witness discussion for fact-level context only

theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas emphasizes belonging and obedience to God. Project default prefers “slaves” where bondedness is salient.

theological_decisions.issue: Distinguishing πνεῦμα θεῖον and πνεῦμα ἅγιον
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render theios as “divine spirit” and hagios as “holy Spirit,” preserving Hermas’s adjectival nuance.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas uses both adjectives; preserving them keeps his diction and allows readers to see how he speaks of inspiration.

theological_decisions.issue: Genitive in τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: faith in the divine Spirit (objective genitive)
theological_decisions.rationale: Context describes the righteous as believers gathered in prayer, not the origin of their faith; ‘in’ reads most naturally while alternatives are plausible.

theological_decisions.issue: Identity of the ‘angel of the prophetic spirit’
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate literally as an angel set over the prophet who mediates prophetic filling.
alternative_readings: Paraphrase as ‘the prophetic Spirit’ without angel
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas’s angelology features angelic overseers; the literal reading best respects his framework.

theological_decisions.issue: Equating consultation of false prophets with idolatry
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Maintain the strong claim that consulting a false prophet about actions constitutes idol‑worship.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas draws a moral equivalence to pagan divination; softening would undercut his exhortation.
‘Deity’ communicates divine essence without archaic overtones; retains metaphysical sense suitable to Hermas’s contrast with earthly spirits.
‘Trust in’ conveys reliance and obedience without narrowing to propositional belief; keeps imperative force.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent, capturing Hermas's tone and vocabulary well. However, there are a few grammatical and lexical issues: (1) In v. 1, the genitive τῶν διψύχων is mistranslated as a direct object rather than an elision of 'the understanding'. (2) The verb ἐπερωτάω (consult) should be rendered consistently in v. 5, 6, and 8, as it carries the technical sense of consulting an oracle. (3) The phrase ὅλως with a negative in v. 6 and 13 means 'not at all', not 'in general'. (4) In v. 19, ἀδύνατα applied to the spirits means 'powerless', playing on the previous 'impossible'.
issues_found: v. 1: 'he ruins those who are double-minded' mistranslates the genitive τῶν διψύχων, which elides τὴν διάνοιαν ('the understanding of the double-minded').
v. 5, 6, 8: ἐπερωτάω is translated as 'questioned' or 'asked', losing the technical divinatory sense of 'consult' established in v. 2 and 4.
v. 6, 13: ὅλως with a negative (ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ, ὅλως... οὐκ ἐγγίζει) is translated 'in general', but it means 'not at all'.
v. 7: 'both kinds of prophets' adds 'kinds of' unnecessarily for ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν ('both prophets').
v. 8: 'less than' for ἐνδεέστερον is slightly awkward; 'lower than' better captures the comparative of ἐνδεής.
v. 19: ἀδύνατα is translated 'impossible' for the spirits, but in this context it means 'powerless' (lacking δύναμις), contrasting with the 'impossible' events.

revisions.from: For every spirit given from God is not consulted
revisions.to: For no spirit given from God is consulted
revisions.rationale: The Greek construction πᾶν ... οὐκ is a common idiom (often influenced by Semitic syntax) meaning 'no [noun] is...', rather than 'not every [noun] is...'. In English, 'every spirit... is not' is ambiguous and often implies 'not every spirit', which contradicts the author's absolute statement. | Adjudicator: The reviewer is entirely correct regarding the Greek syntax. In Koine Greek (especially in texts with Semitic influence like Hermas), the combination of πᾶς (every/all) with a negative particle like ο

revisions.rationale: Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God. Preserve the adverse direction.

value.changes_summary: Refined several renderings for closer lexical accuracy and more natural formal English: changed “ruins” to “destroys,” “slaves” to “servants,” “consult” to “ask” in v.2, “says” to “speaks” in v.3, “any action” to “any matter,” “idol-worship” to “practicing idolatry,” adjusted phrasing in vv. 5–13 for smoother English and closer alignment with the Greek (e.g., “speaks everything,” “desires of men,” “answers nothing,” “intercession,” “assigned to him,” “seems to have a spirit,” “receives payment”). [Regression fix applied: slave restored (revision_pass had changed δοῦλος → servant against DOCTRINE.md policy)]

value.rationale: A low shared seat; “bench” captures a communal sitting surface distinguished from a single chair (καθέδρα).
Concrete furniture term; “chair” contrasts with the bench and underscores the false prophet’s singled‑out position.
Standard, transparent rendering for a claimant to prophecy who is false.
In context, what is being ruined is the capacity to judge rightly; “understanding” fits well.
Project default prefers “slaves” where belonging to God is salient; Hermas emphasizes divine ownership.
Established moral term in Hermas; “double‑minded” preserves idiom and his recurring vice list.
Hermas contrasts prophecy with divinatory magic; “magician” is the clearest modern equivalent.
In context of seeking future knowledge from a seer; “consult” communicates the divinatory act.

source.text: Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους, καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν. καὶ λέγει μοι· Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ· τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. 2. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάγον ἔρχονται, καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς· κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν [καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν], καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν , καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. 3. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς· ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ· ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. 4. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ Κυρίου ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν. ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες· ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. 5. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ Θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος. 6. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον· καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. 7. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.

translation.text: 1. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me, “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful; and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them; and that false prophet, having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they desire.

translation.text: 3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.

translation.text: 4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[a] practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.

footnotes.text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God. Preserve the adverse direction.

translation.text: 5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.

Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ· τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. 2. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάγον ἔρχονται, καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς· κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν [καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν], καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν , καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. 3. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς· ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ· ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. 4. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ Κυρίου ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν. ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες· ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. 5. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ Θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος. 6. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον· καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. 7. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.

translation.text: 7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.

translation.text: 9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

translation.text: 13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 14. [Heaven.]

translation.text: 19. “How,” I say, “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.” “As these, then, are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.

Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος καὶ ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ κατὰ μόνας λαλεῖ—οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον—ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς λαλῆσαι. 9. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος, καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ Κύριος βούλεται. 10. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. 11. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. 12. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις, καὶ μισθὸν λαμβάνει τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθὸν λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν Θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς. κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς, καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει, καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς· κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται. τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. 14 οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί, καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει· οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι. τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
source.label: Mandate 11

translation.text: 20. Take now the power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a man’s head, how much pain it causes! Or again, take a drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground, and it bores through the stone.

translation.text: 21. You see, then, that things from above, though very small when they fall upon the earth, have great power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust in this spirit, but keep away from the other.”

base_translation.text: 1. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me, “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful; and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the slaves of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.

translation.text:
1. He showed me several men sitting on a bench and another man sitting on a chair. He asked me, “Do you see the men on the bench?”

“Yes, sir,” I answered.

“They are faithful,” he said. “But the man on the chair is a false prophet. He ruins the understanding of God’s servants—not the faithful ones, but those who are divided within themselves.”

base_translation.text: 3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.

Yet he also says some things that are true, because the devil fills him with his own spirit. The devil does this in the hope that he might pull some of the righteous away.

base_translation.text: 4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often repent practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.

translation.text: 4. Therefore, all who are strong in their faith in the Lord and have clothed themselves with truth do not attach themselves to such spirits. They stay away from them. But those who are divided in mind and often change their minds[a] seek guidance through divination, as the nations do. By practicing idolatry, they bring an even greater sin on themselves. Anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of truth and foolish.

base_translation.text: 5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.

translation.text: 5. No spirit given by God is questioned before it speaks. Instead, it has God’s power and speaks everything on its own, because it comes from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: no spirit given from God is consulted
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: No spirit given by God is questioned before it speaks
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: A God-given spirit speaks without first being prompted by a question.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and immediate sentence contrast
simplification_decisions.rationale: This keeps the categorical claim while explaining consultation in ordinary English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: having the power of the Deity
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: it has God’s power
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The spirit possesses power that comes from God.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct wording replaces an abstract title without changing its divine reference.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: it speaks everything from itself
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: speaks everything on its own

simplification_decisions.rationale: This natural wording retains both the full scope of its speech and its unprompted character.

The POB grounds this unprompted speech in the spirit’s divine origin and power.

risk_flags.risk: “On its own” could imply independence from God.
risk_flags.mitigation: The same sentence grounds the spirit’s speech in God’s power and the divine Spirit.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 5. No spirit given by God has to be questioned before it speaks. It has God's power and speaks on its own, because it comes from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft improves accessibility, and identifying consultation with questioning is warranted by the sentence’s contrast. However, “has to be questioned” weakens the categorical claim that a God-given spirit is not consulted, and “speaks on its own” drops “everything.” The recommended wording retains the clarification while preserving both the categorical contrast and the scope of the speech.

base_translation.text: 6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.

translation.text: 6. But the spirit people consult speaks in line with what they desire. It is earthly and shallow, and it has no power. It does not speak unless someone consults it.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: the spirit that is consulted
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: the spirit people consult
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: People seek out this spirit to hear it speak.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The passive wording becomes a direct, natural clause.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: speaks in line with what they desire
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Its speech conforms to human desires without asserting why it does so.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This preserves correspondence without adding a motive to satisfy people.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: earthly and shallow, and it has no power
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The spirit is earthly, lacks depth, and has no power.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Shallow” conveys the negative figurative sense of “light” without suggesting physical weight.

risk_flags.risk: “Shallow” interprets the figurative sense of POB’s “light.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording retains “earthly” and separately states that the spirit has no power.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 6. But the spirit people consult speaks to satisfy their desires. It is earthly and shallow, and it has no power. It never speaks unless someone consults it.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully replaces the passive construction and makes the final condition natural for modern readers. “Shallow” is an acceptable contextual rendering of “light” here, especially because “earthly” and “has no power” remain in place. However, “to satisfy their desires” attributes a purpose that the POB wording does not explicitly state. Revising it to “speaks in line with what they desire” preserves the intended conformity without importing motive.

base_translation.text: 7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.

translation.text:
7. I asked, “Sir, how can someone tell which person is a true prophet and which is a false prophet?”

He answered, “Listen, and I will tell you about both kinds of prophets. This is how you must test whether a prophet is true or false: examine how the man who claims to have the divine spirit lives.”

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: how can someone tell which person is a true prophet and which is a false prophet?
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The question asks how to distinguish a genuine prophet from a false one.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Adding “true” makes the contrast with “false prophet” clear in ordinary English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: Listen ... about both prophets
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Listen, and I will tell you about both kinds of prophets.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The speaker is about to explain both the genuine and false kinds.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Both kinds” avoids suggesting that only two individual prophets are in view.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: examine how the man who claims to have the divine spirit lives.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: A prophet’s conduct is the test used to evaluate his claim to divine inspiration.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording clarifies that his life means his manner of living and that the claim is being tested.

interpretive_expansions.pob_phrase: Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.
interpretive_expansions.rendering: examine how the man who claims to have the divine spirit lives.
interpretive_expansions.claim: The instruction evaluates a man’s claim to possess the divine spirit rather than assuming it is genuine.
evidence: The passage asks how to distinguish a prophet from a false prophet.
The command to test him makes the status of his claim the issue.
alternatives_preserved: the man who has the divine spirit

risk_flags.risk: “Claims to have” is more explicit than POB’s wording.
risk_flags.mitigation: The surrounding question about true and false prophets requires that the man’s claimed status be tested.

base_translation.text: 8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.

translation.text: 8. First, a person who has the Spirit from above is gentle, quiet, and humble. Such a person turns away from every kind of evil and from the empty desires of this present age, and regards everyone else as more important than himself. He does not give an answer merely because someone asks him, nor does he speak privately. The Holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants it to. The Spirit speaks through him when God wants him to speak.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: is gentle, quiet, and humble
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The three distinct qualities of character remain intact.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The rewrite replaces an uncommon compound with ordinary English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: turns away from every kind of evil and from the empty desires of this present age
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The person rejects both evil conduct and the age's futile desires.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording makes the contrast natural without weakening its scope.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: regards everyone else as more important than himself

risk_flags.mitigation: The separate clause “nor does he speak privately” preserves the POB restriction in this prophetic setting.

risk_flags.risk: Using “through him” states the human speaker's role more directly than the POB.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording follows the POB's closing phrase, “when God wishes him to speak.”

base_translation.text: 9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.

translation.text: 9. So when a man who has the divine spirit comes to a meeting of righteous believers in the divine Spirit, and they make an appeal to God, the angel of the prophetic spirit assigned to him fills him. Filled with the holy Spirit, the man speaks to everyone there as the Lord wills.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: comes to a meeting of righteous believers in the divine Spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The man joins an assembled community whose members are righteous and trust in the divine Spirit.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Meeting” and “believers” express the gathering and its shared faith in natural English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: they make an appeal to God
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The assembled believers direct a shared petition to God.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Make an appeal” preserves the petitionary force of intercession without formal passive wording.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: speaks to everyone there as the Lord wills
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His message to the assembled people is governed by the Lord’s will.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Everyone there” clearly identifies the multitude as the assembled people.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 9. So when a man who has the divine spirit comes to a meeting of righteous believers in the divine Spirit, and they pray together to God, the angel of the prophetic spirit assigned to him fills him. Filled with the holy Spirit, the man speaks to everyone there as the Lord wills.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and preserves the sequence: the faithful gathering appeals to God, the assigned angel fills the man, and he speaks under the Lord’s will. “Righteous believers,” “meeting,” and “everyone there” are warranted contextual simplifications. However, “pray together” reduces the more specific intercession/appeal to a general communal prayer. Replace it with “make an appeal to God” to retain the text’s petitionary force in clear modern English.

base_translation.text: 10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.

translation.text: 10. In this way, the spirit of the Deity will be clearly revealed. This is the power of the spirit of the Lord’s Deity.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest.
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: In this way, the spirit of the Deity will be clearly revealed.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The spirit’s true character becomes evident through what has just been described.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and immediate discourse connection
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Clearly revealed” expresses the formal phrase “made manifest” in common English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: This is the power of the spirit of the Lord’s Deity.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The preceding description identifies the power belonging to this spirit.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and source-sensitive theological wording
simplification_decisions.rationale: The sentence is reordered for clarity while retaining both “spirit” and “Deity.”

risk_flags.risk: “The spirit of the Lord’s Deity” remains an unusual and potentially ambiguous expression.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording stays close to the controlling POB rather than resolving an undocumented theological ambiguity.

base_translation.text: 11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty and has no power, but is foolish.

translation.text: 11. “Now listen,” he says, “as I tell you about the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and is foolish.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: Hear now ... about the spirit
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Now listen ... as I tell you about the ... spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The speaker calls for attention before explaining this kind of spirit.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and immediate discourse context
simplification_decisions.rationale: The active wording states the introductory function in natural modern English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: the spirit that is earthly and empty
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: the earthly, empty spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The spirit remains characterized as both earthly and empty.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The shorter adjective structure keeps both distinct descriptions.

risk_flags.risk: Modern readers may take “earthly” to mean merely physical rather than morally limited or worldly.
risk_flags.mitigation: The source image is retained without adding an interpretation not documented in the POB record.

base_translation.text: 12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

translation.text: 12. First, consider the man who appears to have a prophetic spirit. He makes himself important and wants the place of honor. He quickly becomes arrogant, shameless, and talkative. He lives in great luxury and practices many other forms of deception. He receives payment for his prophecy, and if he is not paid, he will not prophesy. Can a divine spirit accept payment to prophesy? A prophet of God cannot act this way. The spirit behind such prophets is earthly, not divine.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: that man who seems to have a spirit
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: the man who appears to have a prophetic spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The man appears to possess the spirit that enables prophecy, without confirming his claim.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: Immediate context and POB wording about prophecy
simplification_decisions.rationale: Naming the spirit as prophetic makes the implied connection clear while preserving doubt about its authenticity.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: exalts himself and wants to have the first seat
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: makes himself important and wants the place of honor
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He promotes himself and seeks the highest social position.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB source-driven image and contextual sense
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording explains the ancient status image in natural English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: lives among many luxuries and many other deceits
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: lives in great luxury and practices many other forms of deception
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His lavish lifestyle accompanies a broader pattern of deceitful conduct.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The recast sentence states his conduct directly and avoids the awkward phrase “among many.”

interpretive_expansions.pob_phrase: the spirit of such prophets is earthly
interpretive_expansions.rendering: The spirit behind such prophets is earthly, not divine.
interpretive_expansions.claim: “Earthly” contrasts the false prophetic spirit with a divine spirit.
evidence: The preceding question asks whether a divine spirit would accept payment to prophesy.
The POB contrasts a prophet of God with “such prophets.”
alternatives_preserved: The term “earthly” remains in the text.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 12. First, consider the man who appears to have a prophetic spirit. He makes himself important and wants the place of honor. He quickly becomes arrogant, shameless, and talkative. He lives in great luxury and practices many other forms of deception. He also demands payment for his prophecy, and if he is not paid, he will not prophesy. Can a divine spirit accept payment to prophesy? A prophet of God cannot act this way. The spirit behind such prophets is earthly, not divine.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft substantially improves readability while retaining the passage’s warning against self-exalting, deceitful, paid prophecy. Calling the claimed spirit “prophetic” is warranted by the immediate repeated discussion of prophecy, and “not divine” makes explicit the contrast already established by the preceding question. Revise only “demands payment”: the text clearly depicts prophecy as conditional on payment, but explicitly says he receives payment rather than that he demands it.

base_translation.text: 13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.

translation.text: 13. He never goes near a gathering of people who do what is right; instead, he avoids them. He attaches himself to people who waver and are empty inside. He speaks prophecies to them privately and deceives them by telling them whatever they want to hear, speaking empty words. For he also answers empty people. An empty jar placed among other empty jars does not break; they suit one another.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: a gathering of people who do what is right

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: He speaks prophecies to them privately and deceives them by telling them whatever they want to hear, speaking empty words
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His private prophecies are empty, deceptive, and tailored to his hearers’ desires.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The revision clarifies the setting and deception without making the audience the cause of his empty speech.

interpretive_expansions.claim: Their emptiness describes their inward character rather than a physical condition.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 13. He never goes near a gathering of people who do what is right; instead, he avoids them. He keeps company with people who waver and are empty inside. He speaks prophecies to them privately and deceives them by saying whatever they want to hear. His words are empty because he is answering empty people. spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and its explanations of righteous people, double-mindedness, private speech, and metaphorical emptiness are generally warranted by the immediate contrast and the repeated empty-vessel image. However, it should not convert the text’s association between the false prophet and “the empty” into the stronger causal claim that his words are empty because of his audience. Retain the passage’s wording about empty speech and answering empty people, and preserve the stronger sense of deliberate attachment in “clings to.”
